clue.text: Navy amongst school of whales in body of water

indicators.note: to be amongst a group is to sit inside it, so 'navy' goes inside the whales

parts.note: a pod is the collective noun for a group of whales
N is the standard abbreviation for navy

explanation.surface: A naval vessel finds itself surrounded by a group of whales out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: N slips between the O and D of POD. The whales and navy suggest open ocean, but the definition shrinks it to a small garden feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A pond is a small, still expanse enclosed by land, one kind of watery area.

clue.text: Problems: town's foremost functions involving bar where power's off

indicators.note: the foremost part of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of 'town' is kept
to involve something is to take it in, so 'functions' wraps round the shortened bar
the bar has 'power' switched off, meaning the abbreviation for power is taken out of it

explanation.surface: A town's leading events are hampered by trouble at the local bar during a power cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where power's off' reads like a blackout in the pub, but it is an instruction to delete a letter from the word for bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Troubles are difficulties or worries; both nouns are plural and interchangeable in most sentences.

clue.text: Roofworker heading for skyscraper subsequently

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of 'skyscraper' is used

explanation.surface: A builder working on roofs is off to a tall tower next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading for' looks like travel toward a skyscraper, but it just asks for the tower's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A slater lays slate tiles on roofs, so the trade name is a specific kind of roofer.

clue.text: Topic: Queen has deductive flair about it, on reflection

parts.note: Qu. is a dictionary abbreviation for queen

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the combined piece is turned round
to be about something is to surround it, so 'deductive flair' goes round 'it'

parts.note: a nose for something is an instinct for sniffing out the truth

explanation.surface: A monarch is praised for detective-like insight, as a thoughtful aside.
explanation.walkthrough: Most solvers try ER or R for Queen; the rarer dictionary abbreviation is needed here. Only the flair-plus-it piece is reversed, not the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A question can mean the matter under discussion, as in 'the question of funding', so it is a subject.

clue.text: Surprises husband wearing footwear

indicators.note: whoever wears an item is inside it, so 'husband' sits within the footwear

parts.note: socks are worn on the feet

explanation.surface: A spouse startles everyone by turning up in unexpected shoes or slippers.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes after the first letter of SOCKS. Both words can be verbs, which is what lets the definition read naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: To shock someone is to startle or astonish them, a stronger version of surprising them.

clue.text: I get aboard front part of fairground ride, something taking to the skies

indicators.note: to be aboard is to be inside a vehicle, so the first two pieces ride inside the fairground word

parts.note: the helter-skelter is a spiral slide at British fairs; this is its first half
to cop is informal for to get or catch, as in 'cop a look'

explanation.surface: Someone climbs onto the first car of a carnival attraction that seems ready to fly.
explanation.walkthrough: A helter-skelter is a tall spiral slide found at British fairgrounds; 'front part' asks only for the first half of its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A helicopter is a rotor-driven aircraft, so it is literally a machine that rises into the air.

clue.text: I will enter church or part of cathedral

parts.note: CH is the usual abbreviation for church

indicators.note: whatever enters goes inside, so 'I' is placed within 'church or'

explanation.surface: Someone vows to go into a church, or perhaps some section of a great cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' looks like a conjunction offering a choice, but it is fodder for the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The choir is the area of a large church, east of the nave, where the singers and clergy sit.

clue.text: Accomplishment regarding something local I observed in study

indicators.note: things observed in a place are seen inside it, so the preceding pieces sit within the word for 'study'

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or pore over
on = regarding, about, as in 'a talk on birds'
summat is northern English dialect for something

explanation.surface: A scholar notes an achievement involving some regional matter they observed during research.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' signals dialect: in northern England 'something' is said summat. 'Con' as study is old-fashioned but a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Consummation is the completion or fulfilment of a plan, which is an achievement brought about.

clue.text: Defeat in debate with no opening for amused response

indicators.note: having no opening means the first letter of the word for 'defeat' is removed

parts.note: to slaughter an opponent is to beat them overwhelmingly in argument

explanation.surface: A crushing loss in an argument, with no rebuttal, draws amusement from the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the S from SLAUGHTER. 'Opening' tempts the solver toward a debate's opening speech rather than a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Laughter is the sound people make when something tickles them, a reaction to comedy.

clue.text: Why specimen gets corrupted with last of grime? I was often dirty from work

definitions.text: I was often dirty from work

indicators.note: corrupted material is spoilt and jumbled, so the letters of the first words are rearranged
the last of a word is its final letter, so only the end of 'grime' is kept

explanation.surface: A lab sample is spoilt by dirt, and the speaker admits to often coming home filthy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is written in the first person, as if the answer were speaking; the grime of the surface is exactly the soot a sweep collects.
explanation.definitionFit: Chimney sweeps cleaned soot from flues and were famously blackened by their trade, hence grubby after a shift.

clue.text: Sleep over but appearing upset for sure

parts.note: to nod, or nod off, is to doze

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters of 'but' are rearranged

parts.note: O = over, the cricket scoring abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone has finished napping but looks distressed about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleep over' looks like a sleepover or the end of a nap, but splits into NOD and O. In cricket an over is a set of six balls, abbreviated O.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are adverbial expressions of certainty, used to say something is undoubtedly true.

clue.text: Somewhat unpleasant time dodging criticism is hard

indicators.note: time dodges the word for criticism by escaping from it, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: to get stick is British slang for being criticised

explanation.surface: Avoiding criticism for a while proves difficult and rather disagreeable.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'stick' is informal for harsh criticism or abuse, as in 'taking stick' from the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Sick can mean nasty or distasteful, and the -ish suffix softens it to mildly so.

clue.text: American praise curtailed and retracted? That's normal

indicators.note: to retract is to draw back, so the shortened praise runs backwards
curtailing cuts off the tail, so the word for praise loses its final letter

explanation.surface: An American's compliment is cut short and withdrawn, which is apparently standard behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: The trimming happens before the turning round: the praise loses its tail first, then runs backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Usual and normal are adjective synonyms describing what typically or customarily happens.

clue.text: Scrapping virus alert? Beyond one's authority

indicators.note: scrapping can mean fighting, a brawl that throws the letters of the phrase into disorder

explanation.surface: An official cancels a warning about a computer infection without having the power to do so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrapping' reads as cancelling, but here it means brawling, which is what shuffles the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultra vires is a Latin legal term for acting outside the powers granted to a person or body.

clue.text: Wet weather? Sheep getting mostly lined up inside

indicators.note: getting something means receiving it, so the sheep takes in the shortened phrase
inside confirms the shortened phrase goes within the sheep rather than beside it

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the phrase for 'lined up' loses its last letter

parts.note: in store means planned or awaiting, lined up for later

explanation.surface: A flock of sheep standing in rows outdoors on a drizzly day.
explanation.walkthrough: IN STORE loses its E and goes inside RAM. 'Inside' at the end confirms where the shortened phrase sits.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainstorm is a heavy downpour, a spell of weather that leaves everything soaked.

clue.text: Quantity of vegetation, there being no energy in what veggies decline

indicators.note: energy is abbreviated E, and having none in the word means that letter is removed

explanation.surface: A vegetarian surveys a pile of greens, lacking the energy found in the food they refuse.
explanation.walkthrough: MEAT without E. 'Veggies' is British slang for vegetarians, not vegetables, which is the trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A mat of weeds or grass is a dense, tangled layer of plant growth covering the ground.

clue.text: Investments — Henry to avoid small amounts

indicators.note: the henry avoids the word for small amounts by being absent from it, so its letter is left out

parts.note: shavings are thin slivers or tiny portions
H = henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man named Henry puts his money into schemes that shun trifling sums.
explanation.walkthrough: SHAVINGS minus H. Henry looks like a person but is the physics unit whose symbol is H.
explanation.definitionFit: Savings are money set aside, often placed in accounts or funds to grow over time.

clue.text: A lot of poetry about international name in drink suppliers

indicators.note: going about something means surrounding it, so the shortened poetry goes round 'international'
'name' is put in the result, landing between the two halves
a lot of means most but not all, so the word for poetry loses its final letter

parts.note: INT is a standard abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: Plenty of verse has been written about a famous global brand of alcohol sellers.
explanation.walkthrough: VERS goes round INT to make VINTERS, then N goes in after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Vintners are wine merchants, the traders who sell bottles of wine to the public.

clue.text: Hold back drink over equipment familiar to 17

parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
a wine press is the machine the answer to 17 down would know well

explanation.surface: Someone resists having a drink near apparatus that wine merchants would recognise.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts SUP above PRESS. The cross-reference points to VINTNERS, whose trade uses a press to crush grapes.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppress something is to restrain it or keep it in check, stopping it from coming out.

clue.text: Obligation to work hard? Not right

indicators.note: 'not' tells us the abbreviation for 'right' is absent from the verb for working hard

parts.note: to tire is to exert oneself to the point of weariness

explanation.surface: Is there a duty to toil away? Apparently that would be wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: TIRE loses R. 'Not right' reads as a moral objection to hard work but is a deletion instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie is a bond or commitment, such as family ties that restrict one's freedom.

clue.text: Characteristic features offering pitfalls around IT test

indicators.note: the pitfalls are placed around the test, enclosing it

parts.note: ping is a network command used to test whether a computer is reachable

explanation.surface: A computing exam is full of hidden dangers that give it a certain character.
explanation.walkthrough: IT here is information technology, not the pronoun; the test is a network command.
explanation.definitionFit: Trappings are the outward signs or accessories associated with something, like the trappings of power.

clue.text: Poor imitation of wages that will secure staff

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it inside, so the wages enclose the staff

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: A cheap copy of a salary scheme that promises to keep employees on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like employees, fitting the wages, but it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A parody can mean a feeble or travesty version of something, a mockery of the real thing.

clue.text: Taxidermist with no time for bear

indicators.note: having no time means the abbreviation for 'time' is removed from the word for taxidermist

explanation.surface: A busy taxidermist cannot fit in a job on a bear.
explanation.walkthrough: STUFFER minus T. 'Bear' looks like the animal waiting to be stuffed, but it is the verb meaning endure.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear hardship is to endure or tolerate it, the same as to suffer it.

clue.text: City in which I may broach accepted standards

indicators.note: to broach is to pierce and open, so 'I' breaks into the standards

parts.note: pars are norms or expected levels, as in golf

explanation.surface: A town where one might raise the subject of conventional norms.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside PARS. 'Broach' suggests raising a topic, but it means breaking into.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris is the capital of France, one example of a major urban centre.

clue.text: Greek character — no Catholic, in my opinion, backsliding

indicators.note: sliding back means moving in the opposite direction, so the whole string runs backwards

parts.note: IMO is the texting abbreviation for in my opinion

explanation.surface: A Greek person, who is not a Catholic, is falling away from their faith in the speaker's view.
explanation.walkthrough: NO + RC + IMO is reversed. 'Backsliding' fits the religious surface, lapsing from belief, while telling the solver to read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Omicron is the fifteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, the short O.

clue.text: Favouring air a lot in life

parts.note: to be for something is to favour it

explanation.surface: Someone prefers to be outdoors in the fresh air for much of their life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot' looks like 'much', but 'lot in life' is one's destiny; 'air' is a melody, not breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot is one's destiny or luck, and fortune names that same fate or chance.

clue.text: Stopped, without father getting worn-out

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letters for 'father' are taken away

explanation.surface: A family came to a halt without their dad, who was exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: PAUSED minus PA.
explanation.definitionFit: Used goods are second-hand and have seen wear, so they are no longer fresh or new.

clue.text: Information challenge, implicating male police officer

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: to implicate is to fold in or involve, so the challenge takes in 'male'

explanation.surface: A dispute over information drags in a man who works on the force.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British informal for the facts on something, as in 'get the gen'. The officer is French, which nothing in the surface hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: A gendarme is a member of the French armed police, so an officer of the law.

clue.text: Rest and shelter, accommodated by South Pole initially

indicators.note: to be accommodated is to be housed inside, so the shelter goes between the two letters
initially means at the start, so only the opening letters of the two words are taken

parts.note: first letters of South and Pole
the lee is the side sheltered from the wind

explanation.surface: An explorer at the South Pole takes a break and finds cover from the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South Pole' looks like a place, but 'initially' applies to both words. The lee is the side of something sheltered from the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleep is the body's nightly repose, the fullest form of resting.
